source_refs.note: Exercise 14.4 Q7 (i)-(ii), book p.290 (PDF 295). Answer key PDF 312: 8/3 and 2/3 cubic units, both correct (sympy). Solution book PDF 1279-1281 agrees.

blocks.prompt: 7 (i) Find volume of tetrahedron with the vertices \((0, 1, 2)\), \((3, 2, 1)\), \((1, 2, 1)\) and \((5, 5, 6)\).
blocks.explanation:
A tetrahedron (triangular pyramid) volume from four corner points.
We must find its volume.
Plan: take three edge vectors from one vertex; volume \(= \frac{1}{6}|\)triple product\(|\) (14.4.3).
steps:
Given: vertices \((0, 1, 2)\), \((3, 2, 1)\), \((1, 2, 1)\) and \((5, 5, 6)\).
To find: the volume \(V\) of the tetrahedron.
Method: with \(A = (0, 1, 2)\), \(V = \dfrac{1}{6}\left|[\overrightarrow{AB}\ \overrightarrow{AC}\ \overrightarrow{AD}]\right|\).

Edge vectors from \(A\)
\[\overrightarrow{AB} = 3\underline{i} + \underline{j} - \underline{k}\]
\[\overrightarrow{AC} = \underline{i} + \underline{j} - \underline{k}\]
\[\overrightarrow{AD} = 5\underline{i} + 4\underline{j} + 4\underline{k}\]
Why: Subtract \(A\) from each point: \((3 - 0, 2 - 1, 1 - 2)\), \((1, 1, -1)\), \((5, 4, 4)\).

Triple product
\[\begin{vmatrix} 3 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 5 & 4 & 4 \end{vmatrix}\]
\[= 3(4 + 4) - 1(4 + 5) - 1(4 - 5)\]
\[= 24 - 9 + 1 = 16\]
Why: Expand along row 1 with signs \(+, -, +\).

Volume
\[V = \dfrac{1}{6}|16| = \dfrac{16}{6} = \dfrac{8}{3}\]
Why: A tetrahedron is one sixth of the parallelepiped on the same three edges (a pyramid is \(\frac{1}{3}\) base \(\times\) height, and its triangular base is half the parallelogram).

Check: expand down column 3
\[-1(4 - 5) + 1(12 - 5) + 4(3 - 1)\]
\[= 1 + 7 + 8 = 16 \;\checkmark\]
Why: Column 3 has signs \(+, -, +\); the entry \(-1\) in row 2 with sign \(-\) gives \(+1 \times\) its minor \(12 - 5\).

blocks.prompt: 7 (ii) Find volume of tetrahedron with the vertices \((2, 1, 8)\), \((3, 2, 9)\), \((2, 1, 4)\) and \((3, 3, 10)\).
blocks.explanation:
A tetrahedron (triangular pyramid) volume from four corner points.
We must find its volume.
Plan: take three edge vectors from one vertex; volume \(= \frac{1}{6}|\)triple product\(|\) (14.4.3).
steps:
Given: vertices \((2, 1, 8)\), \((3, 2, 9)\), \((2, 1, 4)\) and \((3, 3, 10)\).
To find: the volume \(V\) of the tetrahedron.
Method: with \(A = (2, 1, 8)\), \(V = \dfrac{1}{6}\left|[\overrightarrow{AB}\ \overrightarrow{AC}\ \overrightarrow{AD}]\right|\).

Triple product
\[\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -4 \\ 1 & 2 & 2 \end{vmatrix}\]
\[= 1(0 + 8) - 1(0 + 4) + 1(0 - 0)\]
\[= 8 - 4 + 0 = 4\]
Why: Expand along row 1 with signs \(+, -, +\).

Volume
\[V = \dfrac{1}{6}|4| = \dfrac{4}{6} = \dfrac{2}{3}\]
Why: A tetrahedron is one sixth of the parallelepiped on the same three edges (a pyramid is \(\frac{1}{3}\) base \(\times\) height, and its triangular base is half the parallelogram).

Check: expand along row 2
\[-(-4)\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \end{vmatrix} = 4(2 - 1) = 4 \;\checkmark\]
Why: Row 2 has only one non-zero entry, \(-4\), in position (2, 3) whose sign is \(-\).
